**Resubmitted as `missing` with a validated operative redline (`ok:true`, minimality passed).**

**Repair made.** The verifier was right that the two cap elements had to be supplied in operative text, not explained away. I inserted one new clause at the end of Article 11 (after § 11.6.3, p0579, numbered **11.7**) so that § 11.6 needs no renumbering and § 11.5 is left verbatim:

> 11.7 Limitation of Liability. Except for a Party's fraud, willful misconduct or gross negligence, a Party's breach of its obligations under Article 9 or Section 5.8, and a Party's indemnification obligations under this Article 11, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the fees paid or payable by AbbVie under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim.

**How each fallback element is now carried (all by operation 1):**
- *Mutual cap* — "each Party's total aggregate liability … shall not exceed".
- *12 months of fees* — "the fees paid or payable by AbbVie under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim". No USD 1,000,000 floor is volunteered, since that sits at preferred and the fallback is the selected target.
- *Indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence, wilful misconduct uncapped* — carried by the leading exception. These could no longer be marked `already_met`: they were only uncapped because no cap existed, so the new cap had to except them expressly or it would have swallowed the currently unlimited indemnities, exactly as the verifier warned.

**Deliberate scope choices.** I mirrored § 11.5 by keeping Section 5.8 (Harpoon's exclusivity covenant) outside the cap so the edit does not weaken us; I did **not** add the preferred-only carve-outs (IP infringement, AbbVie's Article 6 payment obligations) or a fixed floor, as the fallback checklist is the ceiling. Those are flagged in the rationale as the ask if we push to preferred.

**Standing caveat for the deal team**, preserved in the finding: the pre-existing regime is symmetric and mutually uncapped and triggers no walk-away test, so this edit is a genuine risk-allocation trade — capping our own § 11.1 indemnity exposure against preserving unlimited recourse to Harpoon — and can be dropped if the business prefers the status quo.
